newsitem.title: GERMANY: German equities end the day just off record highs.
newsitem.headline: German equities end the day just off record highs.

text.p: The German IBIS DAX share index ended the day on Thursday just shy of record-high levels, boosted by the ongoing strength of the dollar, a calming of inflationary fears in the U.S. and a firm start on Wall Street.
The IBIS DAX ended the day up 19.34 points, or 0.75 percent, at 2,588.04 points.
The DAX 30-share index earlier ended the session up 3.52 points, or 0.14 percent, at 2,570.32 on low turnover.
"The afternoon has gone a lot better for us and I'm pretty bullish at the moment. The dollar is right for us, Bunds are helping and I think we could set records soon," said one Munich trader.
The dollar firmed to about 1.5127 marks and helped underpin trade during the session.
The Dow Jones Industrial index of opened nearly half a percentage point higher, boosting German market sentiment.
The gains came as the U.S. market shrugged off a 0.3 percent rise in U.S. producer prices in August.
Analysts had expected a rise of between 0.1 and 0.2 percent but traders said the data calmed inflation fears because the rise was due mainly to a surge in energy prices.

Among specific shares, Germany's Deutsche Bank AG ended the day up 1.31 marks, or 1.31 percent, at 72.06 marks after news of an upgrade from "hold" to "buy" from UBS provided relief from recent problems with its British asset management unit.

Carmaker BMW ended bourse trade down 50 pfennigs at 867.50 marks, having earlier lost 8.00 marks to 860 after a company forecast that full-year earnings growth would be around the 10 percent level of the first half.
The news was seen as disappointing more bullish market expectations. But the share price recovered over the course of the afternoon to close the day up four marks at 872 marks.
